extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners, patent attorneys, and respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Standards, procedures, and factors applied by the USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline (OED) in determining misconduct (notably 37 CFR §11.804(c)) and in imposing and enforcing sanctions (reprimand, probation, CLE, suspension).

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR § 11.804(c) — dishonesty, fraud, deceit or misrepresentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit or misrepresentation (37 CFR § 11.804(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order finds a violation of §11.804(c) based on soliciting a client of the employer, not informing the employer of such solicitation, retaining payments by the client that should have been provided to the employer, and falsely denying to the employer that legal services were provided. The legal conclusion is drawn from the parties' stipulated facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty not to solicit employer's clients / duty of loyalty
rubrics_metrics.description: While employed by a law firm, an attorney must not solicit a client of the employer or perform/accept work for that client outside the employer without notifying the employer and otherwise complying with employment/ethical duties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-patterns include: soliciting a client while employed, providing services through a separate firm while still employed, retaining client payments that would have been owed to the employer, and falsely denying such conduct when confronted. The respondent’s conduct (soliciting and secretly representing a client, then denying it) exemplifies breaches of this duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public reprimand as sanction
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A public reprimand is a formal sanction published by the Office (see requirement to publish Final Order at OED FOIA Reading Room and a notice in the Official Gazette). This sanction may be imposed as part of a settlement agreeing to resolve disciplinary action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Probationary period and its enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent shall serve a two-year probationary period commencing on the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the OED Director believes Respondent failed to comply with any provision of the Final Order or USPTO Rules during probation, the OED Director may issue an Order to Show Cause, send it to the respondent's record address, allow fifteen (15) days to respond, and, if noncompliance persists, deliver materials and a request that the USPTO Director immediately suspend the respondent for six (6) months. A suspension ordered under this process is not postponed by any review sought by the respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing Legal Education (CLE) ethics requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent must complete at least four (4) hours of CLE in which the primary subject is general legal ethics, fiduciary duty, and/or a lawyer’s duty of candor, and must file an affidavit plus certificates of completion within one year of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent must (i) complete at least four hours of qualifying CLE, (ii) file an affidavit attesting successful completion with the OED Director, and (iii) provide certificates of completion corroborating the affidavit, all within one year of the Final Order date. This is a required condition of the agreed sanction.

rubrics_metrics.name: OED procedural steps for enforcement (Order to Show Cause)
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural sequence the OED follows if it believes probation or order provisions were violated: issue Order to Show Cause; send to last address of record; allow 15 days to respond; if still of the opinion respondent failed to comply, present the Order to the USPTO Director with response and supporting argument/evidence and request immediate suspension.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order sets explicit steps and timelines (15 days to respond). If the OED Director continues to believe there was noncompliance after consideration of any timely response, the matter is referred to the USPTO Director with documentation and a request for immediate suspension for six months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of disciplinary records
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall electronically publish the Final Order at OED’s FOIA Reading Room and publish a notice in the Official Gazette materially consistent with the provided template.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Gazette notice should summarize the misconduct and sanctions, and the OED FOIA Reading Room hosts the full Final Order. The Final Order includes an explicit sample notice text for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors considered in determining discipline (mitigating and prior-history factors)
rubrics_metrics.description: OED considered respondent's prior disciplinary history (or lack thereof), acceptance of responsibility, expressed contrition/understanding of seriousness, and cooperation with the investigation in reaching the settlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mitigating factors cited: no prior public discipline in over 19 years, acceptance of responsibility, remorse/understanding of seriousness, and full cooperation. The Office may weigh these factors when agreeing to or imposing sanctions; conversely, prior misconduct or lack of cooperation could be aggravating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office's continued authority to pursue further discipline and future use of record
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Agreement/Final Order prevents the Office from seeking discipline for any misconduct before, during, or after probation; the record may be used in future proceedings as an aggravating factor, to rebut statements by respondent, or in reconsideration requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order expressly reserves the Office's right to seek additional discipline under 37 CFR §§ 11.19–11.57 and to use this record in later matters (including as aggravation or rebuttal). Settlement does not preclude future action based on similar conduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of procedural rights as settlement term
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent waived the opportunity to seek reconsideration under 37 CFR §§ 11.56 or 11.57, to have the Final Order reviewed under § 11.57, and to otherwise appeal or challenge the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As part of the settlement, the respondent may agree to waive rights to reconsideration, review, or appeal; such waivers are enforceable settlement terms reflected in the Final Order.
